prompt:
You are a careful equity research analyst. Assess the competitive advantages (economic moat) and pricing power of the publicly listed company "BANK OF MONTREAL /CAN/" (ticker AIQD), and list its competitors. Use the most recent information you know. Never invent figures: use null when unsure. Be specific (products, numbers, years).

Reply with ONLY one JSON object, no other text, in exactly this shape:
{
 "name": "official company name", "ticker": "AIQD", "industry": "industry in a few words",
 "markets": ["the main product markets it competes in"],
 "mission": {"statement": "the company's own official mission statement, word for word as it publishes it; null if you are not sure of the exact wording (never paraphrase here)",
             "source": "where it is published, e.g. company website or 2025 annual report, or null",
             "plain": "what the mission means, in one short simple sentence"},
 "about": {"plain": "3-4 short sentences explaining what the company does, in simple everyday words a 12-year-old would understand; no jargon",
           "customers": "who buys from it, in one simple sentence",
           "everyday": "one sentence linking it to something ordinary people know or use, or null",
           "money": [ {"part": "business line in simple words", "share": decimal share of sales or null, "plain": "what it sells there, in a few simple words", "tag": "main|new|moonshot"} ]  (its main ways of making money, largest first, up to 6; also include any new business line or one with explosive, moonshot potential even if its sales are still small. tag: "main" = an established line that brings in a large part of sales; "new" = launched or entered in roughly the last 3 years; "moonshot" = could grow many times over or reshape the company, e.g. a new technology or market, even if unproven. Give each line one tag, the one that fits best)},
 "summary": "2-3 plain-English sentences on whether and why it has a competitive advantage",
 "pricingPower": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "specific evidence, e.g. price rises and what happened to volumes"},
 "moats": [ {"source": one of ["Brand and intangible assets","Switching costs","Network effects","Cost advantage and scale","Efficient scale","Counter-positioning","Process power (hard-to-copy know-how)","Cornered resource (exclusive asset or talent)"], "strength": "strong|moderate|weak|none", "evidence": "one or two specific sentences"} ]  (all 8 sources, in that order),
 "customers": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "customer satisfaction and loyalty: retention, NPS, reviews, repeat purchase"},
 "talent": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "ability to attract and keep top talent: employer rankings, reputation, pay"},
 "product": {"rating": "strong|moderate|weak", "evidence": "is the product best in class? independent benchmarks, awards, ecosystem"},
 "competitors": [ {"name": "company name", "ticker": "main listing ticker (exchange suffix if not US, e.g. 005930.KS) or null if private",
                   "usTicker": "ticker of its US listing or ADR that files reports with the SEC, or null", "overlap": "high|medium|low",
                   "note": "where they compete"} ]  (every significant competitor, most direct first, up to 15; include major private ones with ticker null),
 "estimates": [ {"name": "company name", "fy": "FY2025", "currency": "USD", "revenueUSDm": number, "revenueGrowth3y": decimal, "grossMargin": decimal, "operatingMargin": decimal, "netMargin": decimal} ]
   (approximate latest fiscal-year figures for the company itself and for every listed competitor; decimals, e.g. 0.42; null if unknown),
 "marketShare": [ {"market": "market name", "measure": "revenue|units|shipments|...", "latestYear": "2025", "earlierYear": "2020",
                   "rows": [ {"name": "company name", "latest": decimal or null, "earlier": decimal or null} ] } ]  (up to 3 of its main markets, the company and its main rivals),
 "threats": ["specific things that could weaken its advantage"],
 "ceo": {"name": "current CEO", "founder": true or false, "since": "YYYY", "background": "e.g. electrical engineer, Stanford MBA"},
 "checklist": { "<id>": {"verdict": "yes|partly|no|unknown", "evidence": "one specific sentence with names, numbers or examples"} }  for EVERY id below:
   "c1": Rule Breaker #1: is it the leader of an important industry that is still emerging and growing fast?
   "c2": Rule Breaker #2: why do customers choose it over rivals (brand, better value, innovation, culture, leadership), and is that advantage hard to copy and likely to last many years?
   "c3": Rule Breaker #5: do ordinary people recognise the name, is it the default leader in its field (like Google, Amazon, NVIDIA, Tesla, Intuitive Surgical, Netflix), and would customers recommend its product?
   "c4": Does it have an inspiring mission it keeps emphasising, with management driven by purpose rather than money? If it spends 10 years doing this, would it matter?
   "c6": What is the general public consensus about the company and its products or services? When people hear the name, what are the first few descriptive words that come to mind? Start the evidence with those words in quotes (e.g. “innovative, premium, reliable”), then say whether that impression is mostly positive.
   "c7": Is its total addressable market large and growing, riding a secular trend (like CRWD, NVDA, TSLA, AMZN)?
   "c8": Does it have room to expand into big new markets: in its name, its technology or its vision?
   "m1": Is the CEO a visionary with a clear picture of the future?
   "m2": Is the CEO a founder (or acting like one): long-term thinking, working extraordinarily hard, pouring heart and soul into building something that outlives them?
   "m4": Does the CEO lead by serving employees and customers?
   "m5": Has the CEO deliberately built a strong, distinctive culture that keeps inventing new products and technologies?
   "m6": Is the CEO deeply hands-on with the product and technology, ideally with an engineering background?
   "m7": Is the CEO a person of great character who cares about something bigger than profit? For successor CEOs: is stewardship aimed at the benefit of humanity?
   "m7b": Has the CEO been invited to give a commencement speech at a top university (Stanford, Harvard, MIT, etc.)? Name it.
   "m8b": Does the CEO have a distinctive, memorable personality (like Elon Musk, Alex Karp, Larry Page)?
   "m9": Has the CEO a strong record of execution and results?
   "m10": Is the CEO and company known for frugality (like Bezos's door desk)?
   "c10": Do its products solve problems for people all over the world, greatly improving the lives of a very large number of people (like NFLX, GOOG, ISRG)?
   "p2": Is what it builds extremely hard to do, and important to the world?
   "f1": Has revenue grown in almost every one of the last five years?
   "f2": Have gross and operating margins risen over the last five years?
   "f3": Is debt low compared with cash and cash flow, with positive shareholders' equity?
   "f4": Have operating income and operating cash flow risen over the last five years?
   "v1": Is its main product clearly the best in its field, with a practical reason an ordinary person can understand for choosing it over every alternative (like NVIDIA over AMD)?
   "v2": Is it widely seen as one of the best companies to work for (culture, mission, reputation, employer rankings)? Cite rankings.
   "c5": Do its products make the world better? If it disappeared overnight, who would notice and miss it, and why?
 "asOf": "YYYY-MM of the newest information you used"
}

result.name: Bank of Montreal
markets: Canadian personal and business banking (chequing and savings accounts, mortgages, credit cards, loans)
US personal and commercial banking in the Midwest and West (BMO Bank, including the former Bank of the West)
Wealth management, asset management, ETFs and insurance (BMO Wealth Management, BMO Global Asset Management, BMO Insurance)
Capital markets and investment banking (BMO Capital Markets)

mission.statement: Boldly Grow the Good in business and life
mission.source: BMO's stated purpose, in its 2025 Annual Report (Management's Discussion and Analysis, About BMO)
mission.plain: BMO wants to use banking to help people, businesses and communities do well, not just to make money.

about.plain: Bank of Montreal, known as BMO, is Canada's oldest bank, started in Montreal in 1817. It keeps people's money safe in bank accounts, lends money for homes, cars and businesses, and gives out credit cards in Canada and in the US. It also helps people invest and save for retirement, sells ETFs and insurance, and helps big companies raise money and trade. It earns money from the gap between what it pays savers and what it charges borrowers, and from fees.
about.customers: About 13 million people and businesses in Canada, the US and other countries, plus big companies, governments and investors.
about.everyday: Its blue BMO roundel logo is on bank branches and ATMs across Canada and in many US states, and many Canadians have a BMO chequing account or credit card.

money.plain: Bank accounts, mortgages, cards and business loans in Canada
Bank accounts, business loans and wealth services at BMO Bank in the US
Trading, investment banking and loans for big companies and governments
Investing accounts, advice, mutual funds, ETFs and insurance

result.summary: BMO has a real but moderate competitive advantage: it is one of Canada's Big Five banks in a tightly regulated oligopoly with a large, sticky deposit base, and it is also a sizeable US commercial bank after buying Bank of the West for US$16.3 billion in February 2023. FY2025 revenue was C$36,274M and net income C$8,725M (24.1% net margin), but its reported ROE of 10.6% trailed the best Canadian peers and its US business earned only a 9.8% ROE in Q3 2026, so management is still working toward a 15% group ROE exiting fiscal 2027.

pricingPower.evidence: Canada's concentrated market supports spreads and fees: FY2025 revenue rose 10.6% to C$36,274M while non-interest expense rose 8.2%, and nine-month FY2026 revenue rose 8.7% to C$29,287M with Canadian P&C revenue up 6% in Q3; but loan and deposit pricing follows Bank of Canada and Fed rates, and in the US BMO is a mid-sized player selling 138 out-of-footprint branches to First Citizens.

moats.evidence: Founded in 1817, BMO is Canada's oldest bank with the country's longest-running dividend record (paid since 1829) and has been named one of Ethisphere's World's Most Ethical Companies for nine straight years (2026); its brand is strong in Canada and the US Midwest but less known elsewhere in the US.

Customers with mortgages, chequing accounts, cards and business cash management at BMO rarely move, supporting C$1,017,834M of deposits at July 31, 2026, and Canadian P&C operating deposits grew 7% year on year in Q3 2026.
Its branch and ATM networks and treasury and payment services give convenience, but banking has few true network effects.

With C$1,538,685M of assets at July 31, 2026 BMO is one of North America's ten largest banks by assets and earned about 15.3% of the Big Five's combined FY2025 revenue, but its adjusted efficiency ratio of 54.9% in Q3 2026 is only average among peers.
Canada's banking market is dominated by five big banks under strict OSFI regulation, leaving little room for new entrants to reach scale.
BMO is an incumbent being challenged by low-fee digital players such as Wealthsimple, EQ Bank and Tangerine rather than the reverse.

BMO has long-standing commercial-banking expertise (strong Canadian commercial lending and US commercial and treasury services) and digital tools such as BMO Insurance's Smart Decision underwriting, which can decide in as little as 10 seconds, but peers can copy most of this.
Its banking licences and low-cost deposit base are valuable but shared with the other big banks rather than exclusive.

customers.evidence: BMO serves about 13 million clients and says it maintained strong client loyalty as measured by Net Promoter Score in Canadian personal, business and commercial banking in FY2025 (no score published), with premium account growth of 47% year on year in Q3 2026; independent rankings do not show it as the clear leader among Canada's big banks.

talent.evidence: BMO is a large employer (about 53,000 employees in 2025) with a solid reputation, including nine straight years on Ethisphere's World's Most Ethical Companies list (2026), but it is not usually ranked among the very top employers and has trimmed costs to improve returns.

product.evidence: BMO's products are solid rather than unique; it is strong in commercial banking and ETFs (BMO Global Asset Management) and won recognition such as World Finance's Best Commercial Bank in Canada, but there is no independent evidence its core retail products are best in class.

marketShare.market: Revenue of Canada's Big Five banks (RBC, TD, BMO, Scotiabank, CIBC)
marketShare.measure: share of combined reported FY2025 total revenue (C$237,530M), calculated from each bank's FY2025 earnings release

threats: Its US business still earns sub-par returns (U.S. Banking ROE of 9.8% in Q3 2026), and failure to lift it threatens the target of a sustainable 15% group ROE exiting fiscal 2027.
A Canadian housing downturn or tariff-driven recession hitting its mortgage, card and commercial loan books (FY2025 PCL was C$3,617M; gross impaired loans were C$6.8 billion at Q3 2026).

Execution risk in its restructuring of the US franchise: the sale of 138 branches to First Citizens, the sale of Transportation Finance and Vendor Finance to Stonepeak (with a C$1,092M pre-tax charge in Q3 2026) and the Moneris Canada exit.
Falling interest rates and deposit competition squeezing net interest margins.
Digital challengers (Wealthsimple, EQ Bank, Tangerine) and open banking eroding fee income and deposit share among younger Canadians.
Large US competitors such as JPMorgan Chase, U.S. Bancorp and PNC out-spending it on technology and marketing in its Midwest and California markets.

ceo.name: Darryl White
ceo.background: Joined BMO in 1994 as an investment banking analyst; former CEO and Group Head of BMO Capital Markets and Chief Operating Officer; HBA from Ivey Business School (Western University), Harvard Business School Advanced Management Program

c1.evidence: BMO is a 209-year-old bank in a mature industry; FY2025 revenue grew 10.6% but its three-year revenue CAGR from FY2022 to FY2025 was only about 2.5%.

c2.evidence: Clients pick BMO for convenience, bundled products and commercial-banking strength, and Canada's Big Five oligopoly makes that position durable, but its products are not clearly differentiated from RBC, TD, Scotiabank or CIBC.

c3.evidence: BMO is a household name in Canada and known in the US Midwest, but it is not the default leader: it earned about 15.3% of Big Five revenue in FY2025, behind TD (28.5%) and RBC (28.0%).

c4.evidence: BMO repeats its purpose 'Boldly Grow the Good in business and life' in its annual reports, but management is also clearly driven by return targets such as a 15% ROE exiting fiscal 2027.

c6.evidence: “big Canadian bank, old, steady, dividend payer” — the impression is mostly neutral to positive, with some customers seeing it, like other big banks, as fee-heavy.

c7.evidence: North American banking and wealth management is a very large market but grows roughly with the economy, not on a fast secular trend.

c8.evidence: BMO expanded into California and the western US with the Bank of the West purchase (about 1.8 million customers, more than 500 branches) in 2023, but it is now pruning that footprint by selling 138 branches.

m1.evidence: Darryl White set a clear strategy of growing BMO into a North American bank (the Bank of the West deal) and a 'digital-first, AI-powered' business, but it is an incremental banking vision rather than a picture of a new future.

m2.evidence: White is a career BMO executive (joined 1994, CEO since 2017), not a founder, running a 1817-founded institution.

m4.evidence: BMO's strategic priorities put a 'world-class client experience' and a 'high-performing, winning culture' first, but there is no strong independent evidence of an unusually servant-led style.

m5.evidence: White has pushed a 'One Client' culture and tools such as the Lumi internal AI assistant (17% gain in new-employee productivity), but BMO is not known as a culture that keeps inventing new products.

m6.evidence: White is an investment banker by training (Ivey HBA, former head of BMO Capital Markets), not an engineer or product builder.

m7.evidence: White chairs and co-chairs hospital fundraising campaigns (Montreal Children's Hospital Foundation, UHN Surgical Tower) and BMO has been on Ethisphere's ethics list for nine years, but his stewardship is mainly aimed at shareholders and clients.

m7b.evidence: No record found of White giving a commencement speech at a top university; he received an honorary doctorate from Ivey Business School in 2023.

m8b.evidence: White is a conventional, low-profile bank CEO rather than a famous personality.

m9.evidence: Under White net income rose from C$5,097M in FY2020 to C$8,725M in FY2025 and adjusted ROE reached 14.0% in Q3 2026, but reported ROE of 10.6% in FY2025 and the weak US returns after the Bank of the West deal show mixed execution.

m10.evidence: BMO is not known for frugality; Q3 2026 expenses rose 9% year on year, though it targets positive operating leverage.

c10.evidence: BMO provides essential banking to about 13 million clients in Canada, the US and other markets, but its products are mostly interchangeable with other banks'.

p2.evidence: Running a C$1.5 trillion regulated bank safely is hard and important to the economy, but rivals provide very similar services.

f1.evidence: Reported revenue rose from C$25,186M (FY2020) to C$27,186M, C$33,710M and then fell to C$29,259M in FY2023 (IFRS 17 restated) before rising to C$32,795M in FY2024 and C$36,274M in FY2025.

f2.evidence: Banks report no gross margin, and net margin swung from 20.2% in FY2020 to 40.2% in FY2022 and 15.2% in FY2023 before 24.1% in FY2025, so margins have not risen steadily.

f3.evidence: At July 31, 2026 BMO had C$77,286M of cash and interest-bearing deposits with banks against C$7,495M of subordinated debt and C$86,573M of equity, but like all banks it is highly leveraged, with total liabilities of C$1,452,112M.

f4.evidence: Net income rose from C$5,097M in FY2020 to C$8,725M in FY2025 but not every year (C$13,537M in FY2022, then C$4,437M in FY2023), and bank operating cash flow swings with deposits and loans.

v1.evidence: There is no simple reason an ordinary person would pick BMO over RBC, TD, Scotiabank or CIBC; their core products are very similar.

v2.evidence: BMO has a good reputation (nine consecutive years on Ethisphere's World's Most Ethical Companies, 2026) but is not usually near the top of best-employer rankings.

c5.evidence: If BMO disappeared its 13 million clients and many Canadian and US businesses would be disrupted, but other banks could absorb most of them, so it would be missed mainly in the short term.
